nodes.name: SSF Pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The exposed geometric area of sintered SSF was 1×1 cm². The SSF was ultrasonically cleaned in 1 M HCl for 15 min washed with anhydrous ethanol and deionized water, respectively, and then dried in an oven at 40°C.
nodes.source_text: The SSF was ultrasonically cleaned in 1M HCl for 15 min washed with anhydrous ethanol and deionized water, respectively, and then dried in an oven at 40°C.

nodes.name: NiFe Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: After the pretreatment, the SSF electrode was electrodeposited in the electrolyte containing various amounts of NiSO4·6H2O and FeSO4·7H2O and different molar ratios of nickel-iron. The electrodepositing current density was 10, 50, 100, 150, 200 mA cm^{-2}, and electrodeposition time was 30, 60, 120, 360, 600 s, separately. After deposition, the obtained electrodes were washed with deionized water and dried at room temperature. We collectively refer to the samples of the electrodeposition synthesis method as SSF@NiFe. According to the electrodeposition time, the SSF@NiFe electrodes that were obtained by electrodeposition for 30, 60, 120, 360, and 600 s were marked as SSF@NiFe-30, SSF@NiFe-60, SSF@NiFe-120, SSF@NiFe-360, and SSF@NiFe-600, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniform intensive nanosheet structure forming 3D porous structure for SSF@NiFe-120, while shorter times show incomplete sheets and longer times show agglomeration and spherical particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images (Figure 2) show the structure and morphology of the bare-SSF and the SSF@NiFe synthesized at different electrodeposition times.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS of SSF@NiFe-120 shows dominant Fe, Ni, O contents with reduced Cr compared to bare SSF, confirming surface modification by nickel/iron hydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS analysis images of the SSF@NiFe-120 sample are shown in Figure 3, parts a and b, and it can be seen that there are Fe, Ni, Cr, Mo, and O elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM reveals ultrathin nanoflower-like NiFe(OH)x nanosheets with lattice fringes consistent with nickel iron hydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-magnification HRTEM images of the SSF@NiFe-120 sample are shown in Figure 3, parts c and d. It can be seen that ultrathin nanoflower-like structure is nearly transparent.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows only SSF substrate peaks at 43.6°, 59.8°, and 74.7° (PDF no. 47-1405) with no obvious Ni-Fe hydroxide peaks due to small loading of ultrathin nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of SSF and SSF@NiFe-120 are shown in Figure S2. It can be seen that there are three strong peaks in SSF@NiFe-120 located at 43.6°, 59.8°, and 74.7°.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Ni and Fe presence; O 1s peaks at 530.2, 531.5, 532.8 eV for O2-, OH-, H2O with highest OH- percentage; Ni 2p3/2 at 852.8 eV (Ni0), 856.0 eV (Ni2+); Fe 2p3/2 at 706.5 eV (Fe0), 710.3 eV (Fe2+), 713.3 eV (Fe3+).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In order to better elucidate the electronic structure, composition, and surface oxidation state of the SSF@NiFe-120 sample, XPS analysis was performed, and the results are shown in Figure 4a.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV measured in 0.37-0.49 V vs RHE range at scan rates 10-100 mV s^-1; Cdl of SSF@NiFe-120 calculated as 6.75 mF cm^-2 from ΔJ vs scan rate plot at 0.43 V vs RHE, highest among samples indicating largest ECSA.
